record.paper_title: Open Problems in Constructive Function Theory
record.original_question: Is there an electrostatic model for the zeros of Heine-Stieltjes polynomials that explains their location through a min-max property of the relevant energy functional, analogous to the classical Jacobi case but valid in the general Heine-Stieltjes setting?

evidence.quote: QUESTION 3.4. Is there an electrostatic model for the zeros of Heine-Stieltjes polynomials, describing their location in terms of a min-max property of the corresponding energy?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $A(z)=\prod_{j=0}^{p}(z-a_j)$ be a polynomial of degree $p+1$ with pairwise distinct complex zeros $a_0,\dots,a_p\in\mathbb{C}$, and let $B(z)$ be a polynomial of degree at most $p$. The generalized Lamé differential equation
$$A(z)\,y''(z)+B(z)\,y'(z)-n(n+	extstyle\sum_{j}ho_j-1)\,V(z)\,y(z)=0,$$
with parameters $ho_j\in\mathbb{C}$ determined by $B/A=\sum_j ho_j/(z-a_j)$, is known (after Heine and Stieltjes) to admit, for suitable choices of the polynomial $V(z)$ of degree $p-1$ (called Van Vleck polynomials), polynomial solutions $y(z)$ of degree $n$. These polynomial solutions $y$ are called Heine-Stieltjes polynomials.

In the classical Jacobi case ($p=1$, with $a_0,a_1\in\mathbb{R}$ and $ho_0,ho_1>0$), Stieltjes proved that the zeros of the Heine-Stieltjes polynomial of degree $n$ are the unique global minimizer, among configurations of $n$ distinct points $x_1,\dots,x_n\in(a_0,a_1)$, of the weighted logarithmic energy
$$E(x_1,\dots,x_n)=-\sum_{1\le i<j\le n}\log|x_i-x_j|-\sum_{j=0}^{p}ho_j\sum_{k=1}^{n}\log|x_k-a_j|.$$

Problem. For general configurations of nodes $a_0,\dots,a_p\in\mathbb{C}$ and parameters $ho_j\in\mathbb{C}$, construct an electrostatic model that characterizes the zeros of every Heine-Stieltjes polynomial as a min-max (saddle-point) configuration of a suitable energy functional. More precisely, give a variational principle of min-max type on an appropriate class of configurations (or measures) in the complex plane whose critical configurations are exactly the zero sets of the Heine-Stieltjes polynomials and which singles out each individual Heine-Stieltjes polynomial of degree $n$ (rather than merely identifying their union as critical points of the discrete logarithmic energy).
artifact.status_search_result: Martínez-Finkelshtein and Rakhmanov (and collaborators) have shown that in the general complex setting, zeros of Heine-Stieltjes polynomials correspond to critical (saddle) points of the weighted logarithmic energy and that their weak-* limits are continuous critical measures (rather than minimizers), giving a partial answer. A complete min-max variational characterization that selects each individual Heine-Stieltjes polynomial in full generality, however, does not appear to be established, and the question continues to be listed among open problems on electrostatic models for zeros of polynomials.

status_evidence.title: Critical Measures, Quadratic Differentials, and Weak Limits of Zeros of Stieltjes Polynomials
status_evidence.snippet: In the general complex situation one deals instead with a critical point of the energy... weak-* limit of a sequence of discrete critical measures is a continuous critical measure.
status_evidence.claim: In the general (complex) Heine-Stieltjes setting, zeros are critical points (saddles), not minimizers, of the energy.

status_evidence.title: Electrostatic interpretation of zeros of orthogonal polynomials
status_evidence.snippet: Marcellán, Martínez-Finkelshtein and Martínez-González: Electrostatic models for zeros of polynomials: old, new, and some open problems.
status_evidence.claim: Electrostatic min-max characterizations of Heine-Stieltjes zeros are surveyed as containing open problems.

status_evidence.title: Finite Blaschke products with prescribed critical points, Stieltjes polynomials, and moment problems
status_evidence.snippet: characterizes the solutions as global minimizers of an energy functional
status_evidence.claim: Partial min/max-type variational characterizations are known in special cases (e.g., real, positive parameters), but not in full generality.
